title: "Geese: a fixed effect and concentration dependence"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Geese}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
# The code runs only when the networks are in the cache (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      eval = MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready())
```

```{r compare-helper, include = FALSE}
# MixSIARPFN's posterior next to MixSIAR's for the same model and data
compare_with_mixsiar <- function(fit, vignette) {
  ours <- summary_table(fit)
  theirs <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", paste0(vignette, "_mixsiar_summary.csv"),
                                 package = "MixSIARPFN"))
  rows <- intersect(theirs$name, rownames(ours))
  theirs <- theirs[match(rows, theirs$name), ]
  data.frame(quantity = rows,
             `MixSIARPFN mean` = round(ours[rows, "Mean"], 3),
             `MixSIAR mean` = round(theirs$mean, 3),
             `MixSIARPFN SD` = round(ours[rows, "SD"], 3),
             `MixSIAR SD` = round(theirs$sd, 3),
             check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
```

This follows MixSIAR's geese vignette (Inger et al. 2006 data, as in Stock et al.
2018): 251 geese in 8 groups, 2 tracers, 4 sources, a fixed effect of group,
concentration dependence and Residual only error.

## Load the data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "geese_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = "Group", fac_random = FALSE,
  fac_nested = FALSE, cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "geese_sources.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = NULL, conc_dep = TRUE, data_type = "means", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "geese_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
mix
source
```

## Fit

As in MixSIAR's vignette, Residual only error (`process_err = FALSE`):

```{r fit}
fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = 1,
               resid_err = TRUE, process_err = FALSE)
fit
```

## Summaries and plots

`output_pfn()` takes MixSIAR's `output_options` list. Here it prints the summary
statistics and draws the plots without saving files:

```{r output, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

Each row is a **marginal** posterior. The network does not give joint draws, so the
marginal means of one diet need not sum to exactly 1, and sums, differences or ratios
of proportions cannot be computed from the output. `posterior_draws()` gives
independent draws from each marginal, for plots and per-proportion summaries.

## Compared with MixSIAR

The same model fitted by MixSIAR 3.1.12 (3 chains of 1,000,000 iterations, about 3
hours; MixSIARPFN takes under a second):

```{r compare}
knitr::kable(compare_with_mixsiar(fit, "geese"))
```

Grass, the best-determined source, is close to MixSIAR's in every group, with
posterior SDs about 1.5 times MixSIAR's. The three algae sources (Enteromorpha,
U. lactuca and Zostera) are harder to tell apart with two tracers; there the network
differs more (for example Enteromorpha in group 1, 0.23 against 0.09) and is wider.
The benchmarks in the accompanying paper show how the networks compare with MixSIAR
across many datasets.
